# 1.5 Drift setup

**Epic:** 1, Project foundations (see [epics.md](../epics.md))
**Spec refs:** sections 10 and 14 of [SPEC.md](../SPEC.md) (Data model, Tech stack: Drift)
**Depends on:** 1.2, 1.3 and 1.4 (all done). Ticket 1.4 set up `build_runner`, the analysis exclude for generated files, and the README codegen section.
**Status:** Done

## Why
The local database is the core of the app. Set up Drift before any tables (1.6 to 1.9), so each table ticket only adds a table and its test.

## Scope
- Add `drift` and `drift_flutter` to the dependencies, and `drift_dev` to the dev dependencies. `build_runner` is already there from 1.4.
- Add `lib/src/data/database/app_database.dart`:
  - an `AppDatabase` class with `@DriftDatabase(tables: [])`,
  - a constructor that takes a `QueryExecutor`, so tests inject an in-memory database and ticket 1.11 injects the real on-device one,
  - `schemaVersion` returning 1,
  - a `migration` getter returning a `MigrationStrategy` with only a `beforeOpen` step, which runs `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`. SQLite leaves foreign keys off by default, and the spec's delete rules (SPEC.md section 8: deleting a route keeps its photos, deleting an expedition removes everything under it) depend on them. This applies to the real database and to every test. The create and upgrade steps are added in 1.10.
- Generate the code with `fvm dart run build_runner build`. The generated file is committed together with `app_database.dart`, and is already excluded from analysis (set up in 1.4).
- Add a test helper in `test/helpers/` that creates an in-memory `AppDatabase`, for reuse by the table tickets.
- Update the README codegen section from 1.4, which says Drift "will use" the same tool, so that it says Drift uses it.

## Out of scope
- The tables (1.6 to 1.9).
- The create and upgrade steps of the migration strategy, and migration tests (1.10).
- Opening the on-device database and its Riverpod provider (1.11).
- A CI check that generated files are up to date (1.12).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `fvm dart run build_runner build` succeeds and creates `app_database.g.dart`.
- [x] `app_database.g.dart` is committed with `app_database.dart`, and re-running the command leaves `git status` clean.
- [x] One test, using the in-memory helper, checks that foreign keys are on: `PRAGMA foreign_keys` returns 1. It was written first and failed before the `beforeOpen` step existed. Passing it also shows that the helper, the generated code and native SQLite work together.
- [x] `fvm flutter analyze` is clean after generation.
- [x] `fvm flutter build apk --debug` still succeeds with the new dependencies (needs a JDK, see `project/todo.md`).
- [x] The README codegen section says Drift uses the same command (it currently says "will use").

## Technical notes
- **Checked ahead of time** on a throwaway copy: with the 1.4 setup, code generation for `AppDatabase` works (the first run took about 45 seconds), the generated file passes `dart format` unchanged, and an in-memory test passes. Import only what a test uses: a test that imports `app_database.dart` just to call the helper triggers an `unused_import` warning.
- **Native SQLite in tests:** the `sqlite3` package (3.x) uses build hooks. On the first test run a prebuilt `libsqlite3.so` was downloaded into `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/`, and later runs reuse it. So the first build or test run needs network access, on the dev machine and in CI (1.12). The system library was not what made the test pass.
- **Packages marked end-of-life:** `drift_flutter 0.3.1` itself depends on `sqlite3_flutter_libs 0.6.0+eol` and `sqlcipher_flutter_libs 0.7.0+eol` (confirmed with `pub deps`). Tests and code generation work with them. Not yet checked: that the Android build still succeeds, which is why it is an acceptance criterion. If it fails, or if the current Drift documentation recommends another way to open SQLite on Android, resolve that before 1.11.
- **Foreign keys:** SQLite enforces foreign keys only on a connection where `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` has been run. Putting it in `beforeOpen` means one place covers the on-device database (ticket 1.11) and every test. This follows Drift's documented pattern but was not run in the throwaway check, so the `PRAGMA foreign_keys` test is what proves it. If `beforeOpen` turns out not to run for the in-memory executor, set the pragma in the executor setup as well, and note it here.
- **Dates:** Drift's DateTime storage is a build option that affects the column format, and the spec requires all timestamps in UTC. Decide it before the first table (1.6), with a round-trip test showing that a stored time comes back as UTC.
- **What is tested:** only our own logic. There is deliberately no test for `schemaVersion` (a constant) or for a trivial query (that would test Drift and SQLite, not our code), and the test helper has no test of its own. The foreign key test is the one test. It is written first and fails until the `beforeOpen` step exists.

## Decisions
1. **Generated files are committed,** in the same commit as the file that produces them. A generated file does not count as a second production file (the rule is adjusted in ticket 1.4). A fresh clone then needs no codegen step. The setup itself is in ticket 1.4.
2. **`schemaVersion = 1` here,** with the migration strategy deferred to 1.10.
3. **Shared in-memory test helper in `test/helpers/`,** used by all the table tickets.
4. **Foreign keys are enabled here, not in 1.10,** because the table tickets (1.7 routes, 1.9 photos) test the foreign-key rules before 1.10 exists. Ticket 1.10 extends the same migration strategy with the create and upgrade steps.
